title: The worst creatures are those who refuse and will not believe.
subtitle: When rejection hardens into a fixed stance
then: This opens a passage about those who fought the believers and kept breaking agreements. Ibn Kathir describes them as {trap}those who do not embrace faith and break promises whenever they make one, even under oath.{/trap} The verse speaks of a stance that has {trap}hardened into refusal.{/trap}
now: There may be a corner of your own heart where you've decided: I am not changing on this, ever. The habit, the grudge, the sin you have made peace with. {idea}The danger is not the fall. It is deciding never to get up.{/idea}
old: I am who I am. Some things about me will never change.
new: Refusing ever to change is what hardens a heart. I can stay open.
try: Name one thing you have told yourself you will never change. Ask Allah to soften your heart toward it.

title: They break their pledge every time.
subtitle: Promise-breaking as a pattern
then: The verse describes people the Prophet ﷺ made agreements with who {trap}broke them every time.{/trap} Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}they did not fear Allah regarding any of the sins they committed.{/idea} Breaking their word was not a slip but a habit.
now: I'll pay you back next month. I'll be there on Saturday. I'll call you tonight. Then the month passes, Saturday comes and goes. {trap}Small broken promises become a pattern.{/trap} Your word is a pledge Allah witnesses.
old: It was just a casual promise. It doesn't really count.
new: Every promise counts. Keeping my word is part of fearing Allah.
try: Think of one promise you have not kept. Keep it today, or apologize and set a real date.

title: So that those behind them might take a lesson.
subtitle: Consequences that teach others
then: This verse addressed the Prophet ﷺ about those who kept breaking treaties in war. The aim, it says, was {idea}that those behind them would take heed.{/idea} As-Suddi said: {idea}so they would be careful not to break treaties{/idea} and meet the same end.
now: Your kids watch what happens when you lie to the landlord. Your juniors watch what happens when you cut a corner. {idea}Consequences teach the people around you.{/idea} Let them learn from what you got right, and from how you made right what you got wrong.
new: People behind me learn from what my choices lead to.
try: Think of one person who watches you closely. Do one thing today you'd want them to copy.

title: Even with an enemy, never betray. Be open and equal.
subtitle: Honesty that holds even in conflict
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah's dislike of treachery {idea}includes treachery against disbelievers.{/idea} Mu'awiyah once moved his army close to Roman lands while a peace treaty still stood, planning to attack the moment it ended. {trap}Amr bin Anbasah called out: be honest, stay away from betrayal,{/trap} and quoted the Prophet ﷺ. Mu'awiyah turned back.
now: The business partner you suspect is cheating you. The ex in a custody dispute. The neighbor you are feuding with. {trap}The temptation is to betray first.{/trap} The verse says: be open, say it plainly, keep your hands clean. Allah does not love traitors.
old: If I suspect someone will cheat me, I can get them first.
new: Even with someone I don't trust, I stay honest and say things openly.
try: In one tense relationship, choose honesty today: say clearly what you plan instead of acting behind their back.

title: No one outruns Allah.
subtitle: Getting away with it is an illusion
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {trap}do not think they have escaped Us{/trap} or that We are unable to reach them. {idea}They are within Our power and in the grasp of Our will.{/idea} He links it to 29:4: do those who do evil think they can outrun Us?
now: The thing you did that nobody found out about. The money that never got traced. The lie that held. {idea}It feels like you got away with it.{/idea} That feeling is the reason to turn back now, while repentance is still open.
old: Nobody found out, so it's behind me.
new: No one outruns Allah. What I hid is still mine to make right.
try: Think of one wrong you got away with. Make it right if you can, and ask Allah's forgiveness today.

title: Prepare what you can. What you spend for Allah returns.
subtitle: Doing your part, then trusting
then: Ibn Kathir explains the verse as preparing {idea}as much as possible, according to what is affordable and available.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ said of three people keeping horses: {trap}one keeps it for pride and show, and it is a burden on him.{/trap} The verse ends: {reward}whatever you spend in Allah's cause will be repaid in full.{/reward}
now: You pray for the job but haven't updated your CV. You want to raise strong kids but haven't read with them in weeks. {idea}The verse asks you to prepare what you can.{/idea} Effort is not the opposite of trust. It is how trust looks in practice.
old: If I trust Allah enough, I don't need to prepare.
new: I prepare all I can, and trust Allah with what I can't.
try: Pick one thing you've been praying about. Take one practical step to prepare for it today.

title: If they lean toward peace, lean toward it too.
subtitle: Taking the open hand, and trusting Allah

key.label: What to do with an offer of peace

then: Ibn Kathir notes that when Quraysh sought peace at Hudaybiyah, {idea}the Prophet ﷺ accepted it, and other terms they brought.{/idea} Ali reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}there will be disputes after me, so if you can end them in peace, do so.{/reward}
now: Your brother texts after a year of silence: can we talk? Your colleague offers coffee after the fight. {idea}The part of you that wants to keep score will look for reasons to refuse.{/idea} Lean toward it. Trust Allah with the rest.
old: If I accept their peace too quickly, I'll look weak.
new: When someone leans toward peace, I lean too, and leave the rest with Allah.
try: If someone has reached out to make peace, reply today with something warm.

title: If they mean to deceive you, Allah is enough for you.
subtitle: Choosing peace without fearing the trick
then: Ibn Kathir explains that the believers were told to accept peace and trust Allah, because {reward}Allah would suffice for them and help them{/reward} even if the other side offered peace {trap}as a trick to regroup.{/trap} He reminded them that He had already supported the Prophet ﷺ with His help and with the believers.
now: You're afraid that if you forgive, they'll hurt you again. That if you're generous, you'll be used. {idea}Act rightly, and leave the risk with Allah.{/idea} He is enough for the one who does what is right.
old: If I'm generous and they take advantage, I lose.
new: If I do right and they deceive me, Allah is still enough for me.
try: Make the dua hasbiyallah, Allah is enough for me, about one person you are wary of.

title: All the money on earth could not unite those hearts.
subtitle: Only Allah joins hearts together
then: Before Islam the two Ansar tribes, {trap}Aws and Khazraj, had fought many wars{/trap} with endless reasons for unrest. Allah ended that with faith. After Hunayn the Prophet ﷺ asked the Ansar: {idea}were you not divided, and Allah united you through me?{/idea} They answered: the favor is from Allah and His Messenger.
now: The family that hasn't sat at one table in years. The two friends who stopped speaking. You have tried gifts, mediators, long messages. {idea}Hearts are His to join.{/idea} Keep doing your part, and ask Him for what you cannot buy.
old: If I try hard enough, I can fix this relationship myself.
new: I do my part, but only Allah can truly join hearts.
try: Pick one broken relationship and make dua today, by name, for Allah to join your hearts.

title: Allah is enough for you, and for those who follow you.
subtitle: Sufficiency that extends to the followers
then: Ibn Kathir explains that {reward}Allah will suffice, aid and support the believers{/reward} even when their enemies are numerous and well supplied, while they are few. The promise reaches beyond the Prophet ﷺ to {idea}whoever follows him.{/idea}
now: You count what you have: savings, contacts, health, qualifications. It never feels like enough. {reward}Allah is enough for those who follow His Messenger ﷺ.{/reward} Not instead of effort, but under all of it.
old: I need more resources before I can feel secure.
new: Following the Prophet ﷺ, I have Allah, and He is enough.
try: When worry about having enough comes today, say hasbiyallah and name one way Allah has provided.
